title: The Rules of Active and Passive Voice
body:
ACTIVE VOICE: Subject performs the action.
   The chef cooked the meal. (Subject = chef, Action = cooked)

PASSIVE VOICE: Subject receives the action.
   The meal was cooked by the chef.

Formula: Object (of active) → Subject (of passive)
Passive = To Be (in correct tense) + Past Participle (V3)

Tense conversions:
Simple Present: is/are + V3
Simple Past: was/were + V3
Present Continuous: is/are being + V3
Past Continuous: was/were being + V3
Present Perfect: has/have been + V3
Past Perfect: had been + V3
Simple Future: will be + V3
Future Perfect: will have been + V3
body_hi:
Active: Subject क्रिया करता है।
Passive: Subject क्रिया प्राप्त करता है।
Formula: Object→Subject, To Be + V3
काल परिवर्तन: Simple Present→is/are+V3, Past→was/were+V3
body_gu:
Active = subject action kare. Passive = object becomes subject.
Formula: is/are/was/were + V3. By + agent.

title: Solved Example 1: Active and Passive Voice
title_hi: हल किया गया उदाहरण 1: कर्तृवाच्य और कर्मवाच्य
problem: Change to Passive: 'Ram writes a letter.'
problem_hi: Passive में बदलें: 'Ram writes a letter.'
solution: A letter is written by Ram. Formula: Object (A letter) + is/are + V3 (written) + by + Subject (Ram).
solution_hi: A letter is written by Ram. Object→Subject, is/are+V3.
solution_gu: A letter is written by Ram.

title: Solved Example 2: Active and Passive Voice
title_hi: हल किया गया उदाहरण 2: कर्तृवाच्य और कर्मवाच्य
problem: Change to Passive: 'They were building a new bridge.'
problem_hi: Passive: 'वे एक नया पुल बना रहे थे।'
solution: A new bridge was being built by them. Past Continuous Passive = was/were being + V3.
solution_hi: Past Continuous Passive: was/were being + V3.

title: Solved Example 3: Active and Passive Voice
title_hi: हल किया गया उदाहरण 3: कर्तृवाच्य और कर्मवाच्य
problem: Change to Active: 'The cake was eaten by the children.'
solution: The children ate the cake. Agent (by + children) → Subject. Cake → Object. Was eaten → ate (Simple Past).

question: Change to Passive: 'She is teaching the students.'
options: Students are being taught by her.
Students were being taught by her.
Students have been taught by her.
explanation: Present Continuous Passive = is/are BEING + V3. 'is teaching' → 'are being taught'.
explanation_hi: Present Continuous Passive: is/are being + V3.

question: Passive of: 'Someone has stolen my bicycle.'
explanation: Present Perfect Passive = has/have BEEN + V3. 'has stolen' → 'has been stolen'. Agent (someone) is dropped as it is indefinite.
explanation_hi: Present Perfect Passive: has/have been + V3.

question: Board Exam: 'English is spoke all over the world.' Find error.
question_hi: Board: 'English is spoke all over.' — Error?
explanation: 'spoke' → 'spoken'. Passive voice = TO BE + PAST PARTICIPLE (V3). 'Spoke' is Simple Past (V2), NOT V3. V3 of 'speak' = 'spoken'. → 'English is SPOKEN all over the world.'
explanation_hi: Passive = is/are + V3. spoke = V2, spoken = V3. → is spoken.

question: The results _____ (announce) tomorrow.
explanation: Future Passive = will be + V3. 'announce' → 'will be announced'. The results cannot announce themselves, so passive is needed.
explanation_hi: Future Passive: will be + V3 → will be announced.

question: Choose correct passive: 'They are constructing a new road.'
question_hi: Passive: 'They are constructing a new road.'
options: A new road is constructed by them.
A new road is being constructed by them.
A new road was constructed by them.
A new road had been constructed by them.
explanation: Present Continuous (are constructing) → Present Continuous Passive (is being constructed). Formula: Subject + is/are + being + V3.
